decision.reason: Four interpolation-specific losses compounded. Interpolation.lowerPrepared rebuilt every shorter call child as a suffix shell, including the complete makeChoice(0) receiver call, clearing its existing literal-argument edge. The first repaired selfhost candidate emits makeChoice(i32 0), proving that edge restored, but still omits number and prints undefined SSA: interpolationCallNameMatches scanned from the receiver's first opening parenthesis and selected makeChoice instead of the parser-owned later number target. The second candidate resolves both calls but entry-point result typing omitted kind-10 flow-call nodes, so a signed Int return printed -1 as 4294967295. The third candidate passed the positive exact gate, but an unknown interpolation flow method was still accepted with zero diagnostics and failed only at LLVM assembly. The fourth candidate uses the same emitter call-target resolver during pre-LLVM invariant validation, rejects that unknown method semantically, and retains the positive gate. Direct flow outside interpolation passes, and these issues are independent of C403 mutable storage. Read/hash validation of retained historical baseline failure and candidate success observations. Exit0 denotes successful observation preservation and declared reference integrity checks, not baseline compiler success. Original subprocess exits, LLVM diagnostics, exact controls and proof scope remain in archived records. No new compiler tests, current-source acceptance or speed claim.
